subject: Data stewardship: egress assurances, subprocessors, and DPA addendum request
messages:
From: Sophia Lin <sophia.lin@healthsync.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthSync Legal <legal@healthsync.com>, security@healthsync.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data routing & subprocessors — quick clarifications before sign-off

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. Two quick items from our legal/security team we need in writing before the DPA addendum:

1) For EU tenant data, can you confirm whether any analytics, telemetry, or model‑evaluation jobs will ever be routed to US regions (even transiently) outside a documented failover window? If yes, we need the maximum duration and an explanation of the triggering conditions.

2) Please provide a current subprocessor roster that includes KMS providers, monitoring/telemetry vendors, and any inferencing infra partners. HealthSync needs org names, country, and a short description of the processing role.

3) We saw the draft DPA addendum link but our lawyers want to ensure there is an option to require an explicit egress notification to HealthSync's DPO when any temporary cross‑border processing occurs. Is that something Redwood can add?

I've attached the legal team's redline checklist for reference. Happy to hop on a short call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Sophia
Director, Privacy & Compliance
HealthSync

Attachments: redline_checklist_healthsync.pdf (attachment stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Lin <sophia.lin@healthsync.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data routing & subprocessors — quick clarifications before sign-off

Hi Sophia — really appreciate the clear asks. High level answers below and I've copied Karthik and Jordan who own ops and legal ops respectively.

1) Transient cross‑border processing:
- Our default for EU‑tagged tenants is strict region pinning: inference and short‑term cache/kv are anchored to the EU region.
- Exceptions: we tolerate brief failover windows for availability (configured failover TTLs). The standard SLA failover window is documented as a configurable 72h maximum for catastrophic regional outages. For routine load balancing/analytics we do not route live inference to the US.
- We can commit to an operational practice: any planned transient cross‑border processing > 15 minutes will be escalated to the customer DPO with estimated duration and scope.

2) Subprocessors: I'll attach the up‑to‑date roster. Key ones (examples):
- Redwood KMS partner — KeyVaultCo (EU/US) — envelope encryption for customer config keys.
- Telemetry/monitoring — BeaconOps (US) — aggregated infra metrics; telemetry is pseudonymized and hashed at source for EU tenants.
- Model cache service — EdgeCache Inc. (EU) — edge caching for low‑latency reads.

3) Egress notification: Yes — we can add an egress notification clause to the addendum. Jordan, can you confirm feasibility and suggested language?

I'll attach the DPA addendum draft and the subprocessor roster in this thread. If HealthSync prefers, we can limit the roster visibility to named legal contacts only.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf, subprocessor_roster_2027.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Lin <sophia.lin@healthsync.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data routing & subprocessors — quick clarifications before sign-off

Hi Sophia — quick follow-up from legal ops side.

Proposed egress notification language for the addendum: "Redwood will provide written notification to the Customer's designated DPO and account security contact within 60 minutes of initiating any non‑routine cross‑border processing (i.e., processing not covered under the Customer's pinned region configuration), and will include the trigger reason, expected duration, and impacted data classes."

Notes: the 60‑minute SLA is operationally achievable for planned or automated failovers where a runbook executes. For instantaneous, emergent hardware failovers that require manual triage we reserve the right to provide notice as soon as practicable and will follow up with a full incident summary within 24 hours.

Karthik — can ops confirm that 72h is the maximum allowable transient failover TTL for this customer's EU pin? If we need to tighten that to 48h for HealthSync procurement, flag it and we'll map pricing adjustments.

Thanks,
Jordan
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sophia Lin <sophia.lin@healthsync.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 15:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data routing & subprocessors — quick clarifications before sign-off

Sophia — quick ops confirmation:

- We confirm 72h is the upper bound for an automated failover TTL per current Dedicated deployment settings. That is strictly for catastrophic region outages and is gated by multiple health checks and a manual authorization step for cross‑region write rehydration.
- For HealthSync I can propose a locked profile: EU‑pin + 48h failover TTL (lower cost delta will be minimal), plus an automated egress notification webhook to HealthSync's DPO endpoint (we can stage to a test endpoint first).
- Regarding subprocessors, the attached roster includes country and role. For sensitive customers we offer the option to escrow the roster to legal contacts only and redact vendor contact emails in the public folder.

If that aligns, Jordan — please bake the 60‑minute notification and the 48h max into the addendum language and Marissa, I'll prepare the ops ticket to lock the tenant profile on sign‑off.

Karthik
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_2027.xlsx
